newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China seen lifting 20,000T from Singapore - trade.
newsitem.headline: China seen lifting 20,000T from Singapore - trade.

text.p: China is expected to buy up to 20,000 tonnes of copper from the Singapore warehouse of the London Metal Exchange (LME) by mid-April while shipping large amounts of zinc here, base metal traders said on Tuesday.
"Up to April 15, at least 20,000 tonnes of copper will move from Singapore to China," Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore metal company Donald Mcarthy, told Reuters.
Dealers in Singapore estimated that stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse would fall around 3,000 tonnes when its stock report was released later on Tuesday.

"From the Singapore warehouse alone, it will be at least 3,000 tonnes down. Maybe more," a senior dealer with a European metal trading company said. "There's also more (copper) moving to COMEX warehouses."
"China is buying copper and I expect the amount in the Singapore warehouse of the LME to be lower by 2,000-3,000 tonnes," the general manager of a Japanese metal house added.

The transfer of copper to China began with the report that 6,175 tonnes moved out last Friday from the LME's Singapore warehouse. The volume of copper in the warehouse stood at 46,000 tonnes in the last LME report on Friday.
"The Chinese are buying in large numbers. They have waited enough and they need the material," Kumar said.
Three-month copper was being quoted by the trade at 0300 GMT at around US$2,360/65 a tonne, little changed from the late quote in London on Monday of $2,361/63 a tonne.
"We may see copper testing $2,400 this afternoon," a dealer said, adding the buying should help keep the price firm.
The Chinese buying has helped push up premiums for Grade A copper cathodes in Singapore as they rose to $25-$35 a tonne over LME cash prices from last Friday's quote of $15-$30 a tonne, traders said.
LME copper stocks, on the other hand, were tipped to fall by 2,000-8,000 tonnes when the LME report came out at 0900 GMT.

Metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review copper was forecast "to fall by 5,000-8,000 tonnes." Kumar pegged the fall in copper stocks at 6,000-8,000 tonnes and a European trader said it should go down by up to 5,000 tonnes.
But a Japanese dealer said copper will probably slip by "only 2,000 tonnes".
The Chinese are also shipping large amounts of zinc to Singapore warehouses to take advantage of high prices in the LME, traders said.
"The Chinese are selling all kinds of zinc," Kumar said, adding large amounts of zinc from China is being moved to Singapore.

Traders estimated about 5,000 tonnes of Chinese zinc was due in Singapore soon and another 5,000 tonnes may be on the way. Zinc stocks in the LME warehouse in Singapore would probably rise as a result.
The volume of zinc in Singapore reached 5,675 tonnes in the LME report last Friday, up 525 tonnes from the previous report last Tuesday.
LME zinc stocks, though, were seen by the trade slipping 2,000-3,000 tonnes. They fell 2,850 tonnes in the report last Friday.
Far East dealers said they also expected aluminium stocks in the LME to fall by 5,000-6,000 tonnes. Brandeis sees it down by 3,000-5,000 tonnes.
Three-month aluminium was quoted by regional dealers at 0300 GMT at $1,651/55 a tonne, slightly up against the late London quote of $1,651/53 a tonne.
